clue.text: Tool not working maybe left by side of verge

parts.note: someone off work ill, for example, is sick

indicators.note: the far side of the word verge gives its last letter

explanation.surface: A tool not in use has been left lying at the roadside verge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'maybe' signals that being sick is just one reason for not working.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved blade on a handle for cutting crops is a classic hand implement.

clue.text: Craft everyone's seen in stores?

parts.note: stores are shops
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A question about whether every visitor turns up in the shops.

explanation.definitionFit: These are light open boats, so they count as small sailing vessels.

clue.text: You on a stretcher, injured, weep bitterly

explanation.surface: Someone carried off on a stretcher with an injury is told they will be in tears.

clue.text: City has new actors in new production of Lear

parts.note: the actors in a show are its cast

explanation.definitionFit: The county town of Lancashire is an English cathedral city.

clue.text: Weak tripe dished out at end of month of feasting?

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the month of Christmas feasting

indicators.note: food dished out is served up and scattered, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor tripe served up after a festive month of rich food.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decrepit is worn out and feeble with age, hence weak.

explanation.definitionFit: Prices quoted per person are so much apiece, a usage equal to a head.

the Po is Italy's longest river

clue.text: Quiet person who tolerates much in church — not one to say anything new

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

parts.words: person who tolerates much in church

explanation.surface: A quiet, tolerant churchgoer who never comes out with anything original.

clue.text: Laugh nervously time and time again in row

T again for the second time
T again for the second time

explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a suppressed, nervous giggle, as a verb a small anxious laugh.

clue.text: A name for many an Irishman or Indo-European?

parts.note: Ryan is a very common Irish name

explanation.surface: A question about whether a name belongs to the Irish or a wider ancient people.
explanation.definitionFit: The old term for the Indo-Iranian peoples and their parent language family.

clue.text: Creep involved in phony acts

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A creep caught up in fake behaviour.

clue.text: Unusually solemn broadcaster cut short in Russian city

cutting short removes the last letter

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster

explanation.definitionFit: A historic city west of Moscow near the Belarus border.

clue.text: In light vessel there's a cry from sailor

the old prefix a- means in, as in abed or afire

explanation.surface: A sailor on a lightship shouts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light vessel' reads as a lightship, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lookout's shout on first sighting shore.

clue.text: Simple upright piece in part of church

the letter I is a single upright stroke

clue.text: Matters to entertain English society lady

parts.note: something that matters counts

clue.text: Celebrate extravagantly — after cracking a bottle of champagne?

definitions.text: after cracking a bottle of champagne?
definitions.meaning: a ship is launched by smashing a bottle of bubbly on its bow and pushing it out into the water

clue.text: Certainly not needing the doctor? If you say so

clue.text: New enterprise — a vet gets agent

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so these letters are rearranged

clue.text: A type cut at one side needing a blood carrier

clue.text: They sell many a garment — rich stole, possibly
